title: Exodus Chapter 36 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 36 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 36 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 36.

questions.question: Who were the two main craftsmen mentioned as working on the sanctuary in Exodus 36?
questions.correctAnswer: Bezaleel and Aholiab
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:1 states that Bezaleel and Aholiab were the main craftsmen working on the sanctuary.

questions.question: What did the LORD put into the hearts of Bezaleel, Aholiab, and every wise-hearted man?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom and understanding
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:1 says the LORD put wisdom and understanding in their hearts to know how to work all manner of work for the sanctuary.

questions.question: Who called Bezaleel, Aholiab, and all the wise-hearted men to the work?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:2 records that Moses called Bezaleel, Aholiab, and all wise-hearted men to come and do the work.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel bring for the work of the sanctuary?
questions.correctAnswer: Offerings and free offerings
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:3 explains they brought all the offerings and free offerings every morning for the work of the sanctuary.

questions.question: True or False: The wise men who worked on the sanctuary came from their work and told Moses that there was not enough material for the sanctuary.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:5 states the wise men told Moses the people brought much more than enough material for the sanctuary work.

questions.question: What command did Moses give after hearing the wise men about the offerings?
options: Stop making offerings for the sanctuary
questions.correctAnswer: Stop making offerings for the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:6 says Moses commanded that no man or woman should make any more offerings for the sanctuary.

questions.question: True or False: The materials they had were insufficient to complete all the work for the sanctuary.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:7 states the materials were sufficient and even too much for all the work to be done.

questions.question: How many curtains of fine twined linen did every wise-hearted man make?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:8 records that they made ten curtains of fine twined linen with blue, purple, and scarlet colors.

questions.question: What colors were the curtains made of fine twined linen?
questions.correctAnswer: Blue, purple, and scarlet
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:8 specifies the curtains were made with blue, purple, and scarlet yarns.

questions.question: What was the length of one curtain made for the tabernacle?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty and eight cubits
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:9 states each curtain was twenty and eight cubits long.

questions.question: How were the ten curtains arranged to form the tabernacle covering?
options: Five curtains coupled to five curtains
Two groups of three curtains and one group of four
questions.correctAnswer: Five curtains coupled to five curtains
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:10 shows the ten curtains were coupled in two groups of five each.

questions.question: What was used to hold the curtains together when coupled?
options: Loops of blue and taches of gold
questions.correctAnswer: Loops of blue and taches of gold
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:11-13 describe loops of blue and fifty taches of gold were used to couple the curtains into one tabernacle.

questions.question: True or False: Fifty loops were made on the edge of one curtain, and fifty loops were on the edge of the second curtain.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:12 states that fifty loops were made on one curtain and fifty on the edge of the second curtain to hold them together.

questions.question: What comes first in Exodus 36: the proclamation to stop making offerings or the report about the people bringing more than enough materials?
questions.correctAnswer: Report about excess materials
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:5 records the report about excess materials came before Moses' command in verse 6 to stop offerings.

questions.question: True or False: Moses allowed the people to continue bringing free offerings every morning for the sanctuary work.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:6 explains that after Moses' command, the people were restrained from bringing any more offerings.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 36 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 36 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Exodus 36:14-15, what material was used to make the eleven curtains for the tent over the tabernacle, and what were their dimensions?
options: Goats' hair; thirty cubits long and four cubits wide
Fine twined linen; twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide
Rams' skins dyed red; thirty cubits long and five cubits wide
Shittim wood; ten cubits long and one cubit and a half wide
questions.correctAnswer: Goats' hair; thirty cubits long and four cubits wide
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:14 states the curtains were made of goats' hair, and Exodus 36:15 details each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide, all of one size.

questions.question: How were the eleven curtains of goats' hair organized according to Exodus 36:16-17?
options: Five curtains coupled together, and six curtains coupled together, with fifty loops on each edge to join them
All eleven curtains sewn into one continuous piece with no loops
Six curtains coupled together, and five curtains coupled together, with twenty loops on each edge
Five curtains overlapped on top of six curtains without coupling
questions.correctAnswer: Five curtains coupled together, and six curtains coupled together, with fifty loops on each edge to join them
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:16 explains the curtains were coupled into two groups: five and six curtains. Verse 17 specifies fifty loops on the edges of each group to couple them together.

questions.question: What purpose do the fifty taches of brass mentioned in Exodus 36:18 serve in the construction of the tent?
options: To couple the curtains of the tent together, making it one
To decorate the curtains with gold accents
To hang the curtains from pillars
To fasten the coverings of rams' skins
questions.correctAnswer: To couple the curtains of the tent together, making it one
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:18 states the fifty taches of brass were made to couple the tent together so that it became one unified structure.

questions.question: What coverings were made for the tent over the tabernacle as described in Exodus 36:19?
options: Rams' skins dyed red, and badgers' skins above that
Goats' hair and fine twined linen
questions.correctAnswer: Rams' skins dyed red, and badgers' skins above that
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:19 describes two layers of coverings: one of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of badgers' skins above that.

questions.question: Based on Exodus 36:20-21, what were the dimensions and material of the boards used for the tabernacle?
options: Shittim wood; ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide
Cedar wood; twenty cubits long and two cubits wide
Acacia wood; eight cubits long and one cubit wide
Shittim wood; five cubits long and three cubits wide
questions.correctAnswer: Shittim wood; ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:20 specifies the boards were made of shittim wood standing up, and verse 21 gives their length as ten cubits and breadth as one cubit and a half.

questions.question: How does Exodus 36:22 describe the design of the boards for the tabernacle and what might this teach us about integrity in workmanship?
options: Each board had two tenons equally distant, ensuring stability and uniformity
Boards were irregularly shaped to fit quickly, valuing speed over precision
Boards were made from different woods to save resources
Each board was hollowed out to reduce weight
questions.correctAnswer: Each board had two tenons equally distant, ensuring stability and uniformity
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:22 says each board had two tenons equally distant, showing attention to detail and craftsmanship, which teaches the value of integrity and excellence in our work.

questions.question: How many boards and silver sockets were made for the south side of the tabernacle as described in Exodus 36:23-24?
options: Twenty boards and forty silver sockets, two sockets per board
Ten boards and twenty silver sockets, one socket per board
Thirty boards and sixty silver sockets, three sockets per board
Fifteen boards and thirty silver sockets, two sockets per board
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty boards and forty silver sockets, two sockets per board
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:23 states there were twenty boards for the south side, and verse 24 specifies forty sockets of silver, two per board for their tenons.

questions.question: What does Exodus 36:25-26 reveal about the north side of the tabernacle in relation to the south side?
options: The north side had the same number of boards and sockets as the south side
The north side had fewer boards but more sockets than the south side
The north side had double the boards and fewer sockets than the south side
The north side was made of different material than the south side
questions.correctAnswer: The north side had the same number of boards and sockets as the south side
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:25-26 states twenty boards and forty sockets of silver were made for the north side, mirroring the south side's construction (Exodus 36:23-24).

questions.question: True or False: The coupling of the curtains and boards in the tabernacle illustrates the biblical virtue of unity and cooperation among God's people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The detailed coupling of curtains (Exodus 36:16-18) and boards (Exodus 36:29) symbolizes how individual parts join to form one tabernacle, teaching unity and cooperation as biblical virtues.

questions.question: According to Exodus 36:14-18, what can we learn about generosity and obedience from the way the people contributed materials for the tabernacle?
options: The people gave abundantly, but were stopped once there was enough to obey God's command
The people gave only the minimum required, showing limited generosity
The people withheld materials, causing delays in construction
The people gave randomly without any regulation
questions.correctAnswer: The people gave abundantly, but were stopped once there was enough to obey God's command
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:3-7 shows people brought free offerings abundantly until Moses stopped them when the materials were more than sufficient, demonstrating generosity balanced with obedience.

questions.question: What is the significance of the materials and craftsmanship described in Exodus 36:20-26 for Christian living today regarding stewardship?
options: They teach us to be diligent and careful stewards of the resources God entrusts to us
They suggest that quantity is more important than quality
They imply that only priests should be involved in sacred work
They promote using cheap materials to save money
questions.correctAnswer: They teach us to be diligent and careful stewards of the resources God entrusts to us
questions.explanation: The precise measurements and quality materials like shittim wood and silver sockets (Exodus 36:20-26) reflect careful stewardship, encouraging believers to manage God's gifts responsibly.

questions.question: How does the description of the boards' construction in Exodus 36:22-24 teach about the importance of structure and support in the Christian community?
options: The boards with tenons and silver sockets show the need for firm, interconnected support among believers
The boards' design indicates isolation and independence is preferred
The boards were temporary, so the community should be flexible without structure
The boards were ornamental, implying appearance is most important
questions.correctAnswer: The boards with tenons and silver sockets show the need for firm, interconnected support among believers
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:22-24 explains how the boards were joined with tenons and silver sockets, symbolizing strong, supportive connections vital for a healthy Christian community.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 36:16-18 shows that careful planning and obeying instructions can prevent wastefulness and excess.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The coupling of curtains with loops and taches as described (Exodus 36:16-18) demonstrates how following God's instructions precisely helped manage resources wisely, avoiding waste.

questions.question: What lesson about humility and service can be drawn from the fact that 'every wise hearted man' worked on the tabernacle as stated in Exodus 36:1-2?
options: All gifted individuals humbly contribute their skills for God's service
Only the leaders are responsible for holy work
Work on sacred things should be done for personal glory
The work was done by unskilled laborers
questions.correctAnswer: All gifted individuals humbly contribute their skills for God's service
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:1-2 highlights that every wise-hearted man whom God gave skill willingly came to work, teaching humility and dedication in serving God with our gifts.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 36:25-26 indicates that the north side of the tabernacle boards had fewer silver sockets than the south side.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:25-26 shows the north side had twenty boards and forty sockets of silver, the same as the south side (Exodus 36:23-24), so the statement is false.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 36 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 36.

questions.question: How many boards did Bezaleel make for the westward side of the tabernacle?
questions.correctAnswer: Six
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:27 states that six boards were made for the sides of the tabernacle westward.

questions.question: What was unique about the two boards made for the corners of the tabernacle?
options: They were coupled beneath and at the head to one ring
They were made of cedar wood
questions.correctAnswer: They were coupled beneath and at the head to one ring
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:29 explains that the two corner boards were coupled beneath and at the head to one ring.

questions.question: How many silver sockets were made for the eight boards of the tabernacle?
questions.correctAnswer: Sixteen
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:30 states there were sixteen silver sockets, two under every board for the eight boards.

questions.question: How many bars of shittim wood did Bezaleel make for the boards on each side and the westward side of the tabernacle?
options: Five for each side and five for the westward side
Ten for each side and ten for the westward side
Three for each side and three for the westward side
Seven for each side and seven for the westward side
questions.correctAnswer: Five for each side and five for the westward side
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:31-32 states that five bars were made for the boards of each side and five for the westward side.

questions.question: What is the significance of the middle bar made for the boards of the tabernacle?
options: It shot through the boards from one end to the other
It was made of gold only
It was decorative and not functional
It was shorter than the other bars
questions.correctAnswer: It shot through the boards from one end to the other
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:33 explains the middle bar was made to shoot through the boards from one end to the other to join them.

questions.question: What material was used to overlay the boards and bars of the tabernacle?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:34 states that the boards and bars were overlaid with gold.

questions.question: What materials and designs were used to make the vail of the tabernacle?
options: Blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen with cherubims of cunning work
Blue and white linen without decoration
questions.correctAnswer: Blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen with cherubims of cunning work
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:35 describes the vail as made of blue, purple, scarlet, fine twined linen, embroidered with cherubims of cunning work.

questions.question: How many pillars were made for the vail, and what were they overlaid with?
questions.correctAnswer: Four pillars overlaid with gold
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:36 states that four pillars of shittim wood were made and overlaid with gold for the vail.

questions.question: What colors and materials were used for the hanging at the door of the tabernacle?
options: Blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen of needlework
questions.correctAnswer: Blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen of needlework
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:37 describes the hanging for the door as made of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen with needlework.

questions.question: How many pillars supported the door hanging, and what were their sockets made of?
questions.correctAnswer: Five pillars with brass sockets
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:38 states that five pillars with brass sockets supported the door hanging.

questions.question: True or False: The boards of the tabernacle were made of cedar wood and overlaid with silver.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:20 and 36:34 specify the boards were made of shittim wood and overlaid with gold, not cedar wood or silver.

questions.question: True or False: The coupling of curtains and boards with loops and taches to make one tabernacle is an example of inclusio, framing the unity of God's dwelling.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The joining of curtains and boards with loops and taches in Exodus 36:10-13 and 36:29 forms a literary inclusio, emphasizing unity and completeness of the tabernacle as God's dwelling place.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God’s dwelling among His people as seen in the construction of the tabernacle in Exodus 36?
questions.correctAnswer: John 1:14
questions.explanation: John 1:14 states 'The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us,' echoing the theme of God's presence dwelling with His people established in the tabernacle construction in Exodus 36.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is directly fulfilled by the detailed tabernacle furnishings described in Exodus 36, especially the golden overlay and cherubim?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:14-28 describes Solomon’s temple construction, fulfilling and expanding the tabernacle’s design motifs including golden overlay and cherubim as first detailed in Exodus 36.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'shittim' as used for the wood in the tabernacle boards, and why is it significant?
options: Acacia wood, symbolizing durability and purity
questions.correctAnswer: Acacia wood, symbolizing durability and purity
questions.explanation: 'Shittim' refers to acacia wood, known for its hardness and resistance to decay, symbolizing the durable and pure foundation for God’s holy dwelling as used in Exodus 36:20-22.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 36 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 36 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by the wisdom given to Bezaleel and Aholiab to perform all the work of the sanctuary?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:1 highlights that the LORD put wisdom and understanding into Bezaleel and Aholiab to know how to do all the work for the sanctuary, demonstrating God's attribute of wisdom.

questions.question: According to Exodus 36:5, what concern did the workers express to Moses regarding the offerings for the sanctuary?
options: The offerings were insufficient for the work.
The materials were unsuitable for the sanctuary.
The people brought much more than enough for the work.
There was no skilled labor to complete the work.
questions.correctAnswer: The people brought much more than enough for the work.
questions.explanation: Verse 5 records the workers telling Moses that the people brought more than enough for the service of the sanctuary, indicating abundance in the offerings.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the command to stop bringing offerings once there was sufficient material for the sanctuary work?
questions.correctAnswer: The sufficiency of God's provision
questions.explanation: Exodus 36:6-7 show Moses commanding the people to cease bringing more because the materials were sufficient, teaching the doctrine that God provides adequately and sufficiently for His purposes.

questions.question: How does the making of the ten curtains with cherubim in fine linen and colors (blue, purple, scarlet) in Exodus 36:8 reflect theological symbolism?
options: It symbolizes the unity of the tribes of Israel.
It represents the holiness and majesty of God’s presence.
It represents the diversity of humanity.
It shows the power of human creativity alone.
questions.correctAnswer: It represents the holiness and majesty of God’s presence.
questions.explanation: The description in verse 8 of cherubim and precious colors highlights the sanctity, glory, and divine majesty associated with God's dwelling, pointing to His holiness.

questions.question: What does the construction of the boards of shittim wood overlaid with gold in Exodus 36:20-34 typologically foreshadow in biblical theology?
options: The human body as a temple for the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: The human body as a temple for the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: The boards of wood overlaid with gold (vv. 20-34) symbolize a holy structure combining humanity (wood) and divinity (gold), foreshadowing the Incarnation and the believer as a temple for God’s Spirit (1 Cor 6:19).

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by the elaborate and costly materials used in the tabernacle's construction throughout Exodus 36?
options: God desires extravagant worship reflecting His glory.
The tabernacle was a minor detail in Israel's worship.
questions.correctAnswer: God desires extravagant worship reflecting His glory.
questions.explanation: The detailed description of costly materials (gold, fine linen, precious colors) throughout the chapter (e.g., vv. 8, 13, 34) shows that God’s holiness demands worthy and glorious worship.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the detailed instructions for the tabernacle are merely ancient rituals with no spiritual significance. What does Exodus 36:35-38 actually teach about the veil and its construction?
options: The veil signifies the separation between God and sinful humanity.
The veil was a decorative element with no deeper meaning.
The veil was intended to confuse the Israelites.
The veil was used to hide the sanctuary from Egyptian gods.
questions.correctAnswer: The veil signifies the separation between God and sinful humanity.
questions.explanation: Verses 35-36 describe the veil made of fine linen and cherubim, which theologically symbolizes the separation of God's holiness from sinful humanity (Hebrews 9:3-7), opposing sceptical claims of mere ritual.

questions.question: How does the communal participation described in Exodus 36:3-4 reflect the doctrine of sanctification?
options: Only priests are responsible for holiness.
Sanctification involves the whole community contributing to God's work.
The work of the sanctuary is purely individualistic.
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves the whole community contributing to God's work.
questions.explanation: Verses 3-4 show every wise-hearted man working on the sanctuary and people bringing offerings, teaching that sanctification includes the active involvement of the community in God’s service.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight emerges from Exodus 36:11-13 about the unity and interdependence in the tabernacle's construction?
options: The tabernacle curtains had no practical purpose.
God’s people are called to individualism rather than unity.
The coupling of curtains with loops and taches symbolizes the unity of the people in God’s work.
The tabernacle was poorly constructed with weak connections.
questions.correctAnswer: The coupling of curtains with loops and taches symbolizes the unity of the people in God’s work.
questions.explanation: Verses 11-13 describe the meticulous joining of curtains with loops and gold taches, symbolizing theological unity and interdependence among God’s people in worship and service.

questions.question: How does the provision of silver sockets under the wooden boards in Exodus 36:24-26 reveal God's attribute of faithfulness?
options: God’s faithfulness is shown by providing a strong foundation for the sanctuary.
God is indifferent to the sanctuary's construction.
The silver sockets symbolize God's wrath.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness is shown by providing a strong foundation for the sanctuary.
questions.explanation: The silver sockets (vv. 24-26) supporting the boards symbolize God’s faithful provision of a firm foundation for His dwelling among His people, reflecting His steadfastness (Psalm 89:1-2).

questions.question: What narrative arc does Exodus 36:19, describing the coverings of rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins, contribute to in the broader redemptive story?
options: It foreshadows Christ’s sacrificial death and covering for sin.
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem.
It relates to the Exodus from Egypt only.
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows Christ’s sacrificial death and covering for sin.
questions.explanation: The coverings made of rams’ skins dyed red (v. 19) symbolically point to the atoning sacrifice of Christ, whose blood covers sins, fitting into the grand narrative of redemption (Isaiah 53).

questions.question: What combined teaching do Exodus 36:31-34 and 36:36-38 convey about the sanctity of God's dwelling place?
options: God’s dwelling is built with common materials and no special care.
The tabernacle’s structure and furnishings are richly overlaid with gold, reflecting the holiness and glory of God’s presence.
The sanctuary was to be hidden from the people.
Human effort alone sanctifies the tabernacle.
questions.correctAnswer: The tabernacle’s structure and furnishings are richly overlaid with gold, reflecting the holiness and glory of God’s presence.
questions.explanation: Verses 31-34 and 36-38 show that the boards, bars, pillars, and hooks were overlaid with gold, symbolizing divine holiness and glory dwelling among His people.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's providence and human responsibility is conveyed by the people being restrained from bringing more offerings after the materials became sufficient (Exodus 36:6-7)?
options: God's providence requires human obedience and discernment in stewardship.
Human effort alone is sufficient for God's work.
God accepts any amount of offerings without limit.
The people were punished for over-giving.
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence requires human obedience and discernment in stewardship.
questions.explanation: Verses 6-7 show that although God provided abundantly, human responsibility includes obedience to cease contributions when sufficient, illustrating the balance of divine provision and human stewardship.

questions.question: What theological significance does the presence of cherubim on the curtains and veil (Exodus 36:8,35) convey regarding God's nature and presence?
options: Cherubim symbolize God's holiness, protection, and the throne of His presence.
Cherubim were merely decorative without meaning.
questions.correctAnswer: Cherubim symbolize God's holiness, protection, and the throne of His presence.
questions.explanation: The repeated mention of cherubim embroidered on curtains and veil (vv. 8, 35) emphasizes God's holy presence and the protective guardianship around His throne (cf. Ezekiel 10).

questions.question: How does the detailed craftsmanship and communal involvement described in Exodus 36:2-4 reflect the biblical doctrine of the priesthood of all believers?
options: Only priests were allowed to work on the sanctuary.
Every wise-hearted person was stirred to participate, reflecting the shared calling of God's people in His service.
The work was done by forced labor.
The sanctuary work was isolated from the community.
questions.correctAnswer: Every wise-hearted person was stirred to participate, reflecting the shared calling of God's people in His service.
questions.explanation: Verses 2-4 show that not just priests but all wise-hearted men were called and stirred to work on the sanctuary, illustrating the principle that all believers participate in God’s service.
